Alabaster brick is a versatile material that can work well with natural or artificial light to create the desired effect.<\/p>

Alabaster is a name applied to varieties of two distinct minerals: gypsum, a hydrous sulphate of calcium, and calcite, a carbonate of calcium. The former is the alabaster of the present day. The latter is generally the one known to the ancients.<\/p>
\n

The two kinds are readily distinguished by their relative hardnesses. The gypsum kind is soft enough to be scratched by a fingernail, with a hardness of 1.5 to 2. The calcite kind is too hard to be scratched in this way, with a hardness of 3, though it does yield readily to a knife.
